```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)

set.seed(2024)

# ── Consistent color palette across all figures ───────────────────────────
pal <- c(
  baseline = "#8B9DB5",
  flu      = "#E55C30",
  rsv      = "#27AE60",
  covid    = "#A93226"
)

# ── Shared ggplot theme ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
theme_ts <- function(...) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      axis.title.x       = element_blank(),
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      legend.title       = element_blank(),
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 10)
    ) +
    theme(...)
}
```

## Pre-Pandemic Data (2010–2019)

```{r fig2-data}
# Pre-pandemic data (2010–2019) — all analyses use this dataset
n2     <- 522  # ~10 years of weekly data
dates2 <- seq(as.Date("2010-01-03"), by = "week", length.out = n2)
t2     <- seq_len(n2)
wk2    <- as.integer(format(dates2, "%U"))

# ── Influenza: year-to-year variation in peak timing and intensity ─────────
# Assign each week to a flu season (Jul Y → Jun Y+1, labelled Y+1)
flu_season_yr <- as.integer(format(dates2, "%Y")) +
                 ifelse(as.integer(format(dates2, "%m")) >= 7L, 1L, 0L)
seasons   <- sort(unique(flu_season_yr))
n_seasons <- length(seasons)

# Each season: random ±3-week peak shift and log-normal amplitude multiplier
peak_offsets <- round(rnorm(n_seasons, 0, 2.5))   # SD ≈ 2–3 weeks
amplitudes   <- exp(rnorm(n_seasons, 0, 0.45))    # ~50 % CV in intensity

flu2 <- numeric(n2)
for (i in seq_along(seasons)) {
  idx  <- which(flu_season_yr == seasons[i])
  pw   <- 2L + peak_offsets[i]               # typical peak week 2 ± shift
  flu2[idx] <- pmax(0, cos(2 * pi * (wk2[idx] - pw) / 52))^5 *
               90 * amplitudes[i]             # ^5 gives sharper winter spike
}
flu2 <- pmax(0, flu2 + rnorm(n2, 0, 4))

# ── RSV: weak biennial variation (higher/lower amplitude in alternate years)
rsv_year    <- as.integer(format(dates2, "%Y"))
biennl_mult <- ifelse(rsv_year %% 2 == 0, 1.40, 0.65)
rsv2 <- pmax(0,
  pmax(0, cos(2 * pi * (wk2 - 47) / 52))^2.5 * 55 * biennl_mult + rnorm(n2, 0, 3)
)

# ── Scale to [0, 1] for model predictors ──────────────────────────────────
flu2_s <- flu2 / max(flu2)
rsv2_s <- rsv2 / max(rsv2)

# ── Harmonic terms ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sin1_2 <- sin(2 * pi * t2 / 52);  cos1_2 <- cos(2 * pi * t2 / 52)
sin2_2 <- sin(4 * pi * t2 / 52);  cos2_2 <- cos(4 * pi * t2 / 52)

# ── Pneumonia: no long-term trend; strong flu spike; low overdispersion ───
log_mu2 <- (5.50 +
             0.45 * sin1_2 - 0.32 * cos1_2 +   # harmonic amplitude ≈ 0.55
             0.12 * sin2_2 + 0.05 * cos2_2 +
             1.00 * flu2_s + 0.45 * rsv2_s)     # flu log-RR raised to 1.0

pneu2 <- rnbinom(n2, mu = exp(log_mu2), size = 40)  # size↑ → cleaner signal

df2 <- tibble(
  date  = dates2,
  t     = t2,
  pneu  = pneu2,
  flu   = flu2, rsv = rsv2,
  flu_s = flu2_s, rsv_s = rsv2_s,
  sin1  = sin1_2, cos1 = cos1_2,
  sin2  = sin2_2, cos2 = cos2_2
)

winters2 <- tibble(
  xmin = as.Date(paste0(2009:2018, "-12-01")),
  xmax = as.Date(c(paste0(2010:2018, "-02-28"), "2019-02-28"))
)
```

## Figure 1: The Raw Input Data

```{r fig1}
#| fig-cap: "Weekly time series for each variable, 2010–2019 (pre-pandemic). Blue bands mark winter months (December–February), when respiratory viruses tend to peak."
#| fig-height: 7

# Long format: one row per date × series (pre-pandemic data only)
df_long1 <- df2 |>
  select(date, pneu, flu, rsv) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    panel = factor(series,
      levels = c("pneu", "flu", "rsv"),
      labels = c(
        "Pneumonia Hospitalizations  (weekly count)",
        "Influenza Activity  (index, 0 – 100)",
        "RSV Activity  (index, 0 – 100)"
      )
    ),
    color = case_match(series,
      "pneu" ~ "black",
      "flu"  ~ unname(pal["flu"]),
      "rsv"  ~ unname(pal["rsv"])
    )
  )

ggplot(df_long1, aes(date, value)) +
  geom_rect(
    data        = winters2,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill        = "steelblue", alpha = 0.09
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(color = color), linewidth = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(y = NULL, title = "Figure 1: Raw Input Data  (2010–2019)") +
  theme_ts(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11)
  )
```

## Model Fitting

```{r fit-model}
# ── Fit Poisson GLM on pre-pandemic data (no COVID term) ──────────────────
fit <- glm(
  pneu ~ sin1 + cos1 + sin2 + cos2 + flu_s + rsv_s,
  data   = df2,
  family = poisson(link = "log")
)

# Fitted values and 95% pointwise CI on the mean
pred <- predict(fit, se.fit = TRUE)
df2 <- df2 |>
  mutate(
    fitted    = exp(pred$fit),
    fit_lo    = exp(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit),
    fit_hi    = exp(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit),
    pearson_r = residuals(fit, type = "pearson")
  )

# ── Decompose fitted values into additive components ─────────────────────
b <- coef(fit)

lp_base     <- b["(Intercept)"]
lp_seasonal <- b["sin1"]*df2$sin1 + b["cos1"]*df2$cos1 +
               b["sin2"]*df2$sin2 + b["cos2"]*df2$cos2
lp_flu      <- b["flu_s"] * df2$flu_s
lp_rsv      <- b["rsv_s"] * df2$rsv_s

mu_none <- exp(lp_base + lp_seasonal)                  # no viruses
mu_rsv  <- exp(lp_base + lp_seasonal + lp_rsv)         # +RSV
mu_full <- df2$fitted                                   # +RSV +flu

df2 <- df2 |>
  mutate(
    comp_baseline = mu_none,
    comp_rsv      = pmax(0, mu_rsv  - mu_none),
    comp_flu      = pmax(0, mu_full - mu_rsv)
  )
```

## Figure 5: Decomposing the Signal

```{r fig5}
#| fig-cap: "Stacked area chart showing the contribution of each model component to weekly expected hospitalizations. The total stack matches the model's fitted values at every time point. Observed counts are overlaid as black points."

decomp_long <- df2 |>
  select(date, pneu, comp_baseline, comp_rsv, comp_flu) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = starts_with("comp_"),
    names_to  = "component",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(component = factor(component,
    levels = c("comp_baseline", "comp_rsv", "comp_flu"),
    labels = c("Seasonal Baseline", "RSV", "Influenza")
  ))

comp_colors <- c(
  "Seasonal Baseline" = unname(pal["baseline"]),
  "RSV"               = unname(pal["rsv"]),
  "Influenza"         = unname(pal["flu"])
)

ggplot(decomp_long, aes(date, value, fill = component)) +
  geom_rect(
    data        = winters2,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill        = "white", alpha = 0.35
  ) +
  geom_area(position = "stack", alpha = 0.88, color = NA) +
  geom_point(
    data        = df2,
    aes(x = date, y = pneu),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color       = "black", size = 0.75, alpha = 0.50
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = comp_colors) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format()) +
  labs(
    y        = "Expected hospitalizations / week",
    title    = "Figure 5: Decomposing Pneumonia Hospitalizations by Component",
    subtitle = "Stacked areas = model components; points = observed counts",
    fill     = NULL
  ) +
  theme_ts() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, reverse = TRUE))
```

## Figure 6: Attributable Burden Summary

```{r fig6}
#| fig-cap: "Estimated hospitalizations attributable to each respiratory virus over the full 10-year pre-pandemic period (excess above the seasonal baseline). Percentages are of total modeled hospitalizations."
#| fig-height: 3.8

virus_totals <- tibble(
  Component = c("Influenza", "RSV"),
  Total     = c(sum(df2$comp_flu), sum(df2$comp_rsv)),
  Color     = c(pal["flu"], pal["rsv"])
) |>
  mutate(
    pct_total = Total / sum(df2$fitted) * 100,
    bar_label = sprintf(
      "%s hospitalizations  (%.1f%% of total)",
      comma(round(Total)),
      pct_total
    ),
    Component = fct_reorder(Component, Total)
  )

ggplot(virus_totals, aes(x = Component, y = Total, fill = Color)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = bar_label),
    hjust  = -0.05,
    size   = 3.8,
    fontface = "bold",
    color  = "gray20"
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma_format(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.55))
  ) +
  labs(
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Estimated attributable hospitalizations  (10-year total)",
    title    = "Figure 6: Virus-Attributable Hospitalization Burden",
    subtitle = "Excess hospitalizations above seasonal baseline, by pathogen"
  ) +
  theme_ts(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray88"),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.margin        = margin(10, 120, 10, 10)
  )
```
